dimensions.label: Adaptation
dimensions.question: When is flexibility wisdom, and when is it surrender?

dimensions.label: Agency
dimensions.question: Who is acting, and who is being used as an instrument?

dimensions.label: Legitimacy
dimensions.question: Why do people accept someone's right to rule?

dimensions.label: Mastery
dimensions.question: What does earned competence require—and what can imitate it?

dimensions.label: Power
dimensions.question: Who benefits, who pays, and who gets to define the game?

dimensions.label: Representation
dimensions.question: How faithfully does a system turn people into voice?

dimensions.label: Absurdity
dimensions.question: How do we remain human inside systems that refuse to make sense?

dimensions.label: Otherness
dimensions.question: What happens when we meet a mind, culture, or model unlike our own?

nodes.title: I Want to Believe
nodes.summary: Spielberg, Disclosure Day, and the hopeful danger of mistaking our model of the world for the world itself.
nodes.question: Can wonder survive contact with an intelligence that does not share our categories?

nodes.title: The Fuzzy Logic of Nolan’s Odyssey
nodes.summary: The Ship of Theseus, the Sorites paradox, and how Nolan betrays Homer faithfully.
nodes.question: Can changing a classic be the most faithful way to preserve it?

nodes.title: Many-Turning, Never-Bending
nodes.summary: Odysseus and Ajax as competing selves: strategic adaptation against uncompromising principle.
nodes.question: How do you win the game without becoming what the game rewards?

nodes.title: Agile Is a Theory of Knowledge
nodes.summary: Agile works when it is a disciplined response to uncertainty, not a calendar full of renamed meetings.
nodes.question: What if adaptation is not the absence of principle but a principle about incomplete knowledge?

nodes.title: Choose the Right Hard Thing
nodes.summary: Mastery grows through chosen difficulty; impostor syndrome and false confidence are both failures to read the evidence clearly.
nodes.question: Which difficulty produces capability, and which merely performs suffering?

nodes.title: Which Half Is the Horse?
nodes.summary: Automation can extend human judgment—or conscript humans into serving the machine's blind spots.
nodes.question: Does the tool enlarge human agency, or does the human become its error-handling subsystem?

nodes.title: The People's House Got Too Small
nodes.summary: A systems-level exploration of House size, proportional voice, districting, terms, age cohorts, and electoral incentives.
nodes.question: What would representation look like if we designed it for the represented?

nodes.title: Who Has the Right to Rule?
nodes.summary: From Aragorn to Paul Atreides, stories teach us to recognize legitimate kings and applaud charismatic tyrants—sometimes in the same breath.
nodes.question: Why does inherited authority feel safer than revolutionary charisma until it suddenly doesn't?

nodes.title: Don't Panic Is an Ethical System
nodes.summary: Douglas Adams makes grace under cosmic nonsense feel less like denial and more like moral style.
nodes.question: What do we owe one another when the universe refuses to supply a sensible plot?

nodes.title: The Map Is Not the Territory
nodes.summary: Every model clarifies by leaving something out; trouble begins when usefulness hardens into certainty.
nodes.question: Which parts of reality did this useful model teach us not to see?

nodes.title: Principled Adaptation
nodes.summary: Hold values firmly, hypotheses lightly, and tactics loosely enough to learn from contact with reality.
nodes.question: What must remain fixed so that everything else can change?

nodes.title: Earned Competence
nodes.summary: Capability is evidence accumulated through repeated contact with consequential work, not merely a credential or a feeling.
nodes.question: What evidence should count when formal channels and actual ability disagree?

nodes.title: Human Agency
nodes.summary: Tools and institutions should increase a person's capacity to perceive, decide, and act—not just increase throughput.
nodes.question: Who can still say no, change course, or understand the consequence?

nodes.title: Making Reality Legible
nodes.summary: Good leadership builds a shared model of reality without confusing the dashboard for the world.
nodes.question: Can a system become understandable without flattening the people inside it?

nodes.title: Enshittification
nodes.summary: Cory Doctorow's account of platforms shifting value from users to business customers and finally to themselves.
nodes.question: What incentive makes a useful system begin consuming the people who depend on it?

nodes.title: Greek Heroes as Operating Systems
nodes.summary: Odysseus, Ajax, Achilles, Heracles, and Perseus embody strengths whose excess becomes fate.
nodes.question: Which virtue becomes your tragedy when you cannot stop performing it?

nodes.title: Dune's Charismatic Trap
nodes.summary: Herbert gives us a leader engineered to command belief and asks whether recognizing the trap is enough to escape it.
nodes.question: Why do warnings about charismatic power so often become advertisements for it?

nodes.title: The Return of the King
nodes.summary: Tolkien restores rightful rule by joining inheritance to sacrifice, restraint, service, and recognition.
nodes.question: What transforms a blood claim into a moral claim?

edges.reason: The essay's central warning is that our categories are useful maps, not the outer boundary of reality.
Both ask how a familiar story changes when it meets the needs and fears of a different present.
Spielberg's wonder and Adams's composure offer different humane responses to an unknowable universe.
An adaptation becomes a new model of an old work, revealing what the present notices and what it omits.
Agile begins with the premise that a plan is a revisable model, not reality under command.
Making systems legible is necessary, but every simplification creates blind spots that leadership must remember.
The modern film opens naturally into the older argument over Odysseus's flexibility, costs, and character.
The epic becomes more legible when its heroes are read as virtues pushed toward catastrophic excess.
Odysseus and Ajax are the sharpest contrast between many-turning intelligence and the refusal to bend.
The apparent choice between cunning and rigidity becomes a search for values that survive tactical change.
The personal tension between principle and flexibility reappears professionally as adaptation under uncertainty.
Agile is coherent when fixed values guide flexible hypotheses, plans, and tactics.
Deliberate practice is adaptation with a spine: feedback changes technique while purpose remains stable.
Iteration only compounds when the work is difficult enough to produce honest feedback and new capability.
A delivery system improves when it makes uncertainty, tradeoffs, and learning visible to the people acting within it.
Chosen difficulty matters because it leaves behind evidence: judgment, skill, and a longer record of solved problems.
Automation can remove drudgery, but it can also remove the difficulty through which people acquire judgment.
A system that automates decisions while assigning humans only the failures erodes both learning and responsibility.
The useful measure of automation is not task completion alone but the agency left with the human participant.
Both name systems that begin by serving people and end by reorganizing people around institutional extraction.
Platform decay and institutional drift share a question: which incentives separate a system from the people it claims to serve?
Political representation is a mechanism for converting individual agency into collective power.
People can act responsibly only when the systems shaping their choices are understandable enough to contest.
Reform begins by making the mismatch between population, districts, terms, and political voice visible.
Mechanics of representation sit inside the older problem of why a population recognizes rule as rightful.
Dune treats popular devotion and extraordinary competence as accelerants of tyranny rather than proof of legitimacy.
Aragorn offers the opposite construction: inherited authority disciplined by restraint, service, and earned recognition.
Placed together, Paul and Aragorn expose how similar heroic grammar can produce radically different theories of rule.
When control is impossible, composure, generosity, and style remain small but genuine forms of agency.
Adams punctures the grandeur through which rulers and institutions persuade us that their arrangements are cosmically necessary.
